text: Over the past two years, organisations like the Media Literacy Council have also supported ground-up projects to help the public become better-informed consumers through its Better Internet x Youth Call-for-Proposals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To educate citizens and businesses on good cyber hygiene, CSA launched a cybersecurity awareness campaign in May 2018, called "Cyber Tips 4 You".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It reaches out to businesses on good cybersecurity practices through a variety of channels, such as talks, conferences and an online portal called "GoSafeOnline".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: CSA and IMDA are also working with schools to help students pick up essential cybersecurity knowledge and learn to effectively protect themselves from an early age.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have launched Digital Defence as the sixth pillar of Total Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Like our battle against terrorism, we need everyone to play their part.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This means being secure, alert and responsible online.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There are five things we can all do, including Members of this House, to make vigilance against deliberate online falsehoods and good cyber hygiene a matter of personal responsibility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These five practices go a long way to help all of us guard against fake news, and stay safe online.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Vikram Nair asked how we assess the cybersecurity of our Government systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: A safe and trusted cyberspace is essential for Smart Nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This includes strengthening partnerships between the Government and industry, to achieve a higher level of collective cybersecurity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will need the combined efforts of our stakeholders, that is, industry, academia and the community to achieve this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One of the many ways that we do this is through the Government Bug Bounty Programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We gained insights into potential attack vectors, better secured our web applications, and improved our mechanisms for patching vulnerabilities effectively and comprehensively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Seven out of the top 10 awarded bounty participants were from Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will conduct more of such programmes in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I hope some of the participants apply for jobs at CSA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Teo Ser Luck asked about our targeted efforts to seize new opportunities in the digital economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Cybersecurity is an area of economic opportunity that complements Singapore’s existing strengths – strong connectivity, a digitally savvy workforce, and a reputation for trust and transparency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: A strong cybersecurity ecosystem will provide expertise and solutions that contribute to a more resilient digital infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are helping cybersecurity startups scale and establish their credentials through the Innovation Cybersecurity Ecosystem at Block71 (ICE71), which brings together a community of entrepreneurs, investors and corporate partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The community has done well since its launch last year, reaching out to more than 50,000 people through various events.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are starting to see a growth of local cybersecurity startups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One such company is The Cyber Assembly, a homegrown startup that connects people to cyber skills through an active learning cyber range, bootcamp programmes, and even a mobile game called “What the Hack”.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: ICE71’s Scale programme provided opportunities for Mr Ng Pan Yong, the company’s founder, to connect with the right audience and grow his business.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In September 2018, CSA launched an Industry Call for Innovation to catalyse the development and adoption of innovative cybersecurity solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: CSA received more than 70 proposals to develop solutions for 10 cybersecurity challenge statements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Low Thia Khiang asked how we are meeting Singapore's cybersecurity manpower needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Building a strong cybersecurity workforce is important not only for the development of our cybersecurity industry, but also for our national security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As our world becomes more connected and new cyber threats emerge, demand for cybersecurity talent has grown exponentially.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: At the same time, the actual number of cybersecurity professionals in employment quadrupled to 4,900, which is about 3% of the ICT workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We expect the strong demand for cybersecurity professionals to continue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our agencies are working closely with one another on the cybersecurity ecosystem to strengthen the pipeline of cybersecurity professionals, deepen their skills and technical expertise, and improve the career progression and recognition for the profession.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To meet industry needs, IMDA and CSA drive targeted efforts under the TechSkills Accelerator (TeSA) initiative.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These include the Cyber Security Associates and Technologists Programme which develops and upskills fresh and mid-career professionals for cybersecurity jobs through on-the-job training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In addition, over 3,000 individuals have benefited from 50 cybersecurity courses supported under TeSA's Critical Information Technology Resource Programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To attract, develop and retain cybersecurity practitioners in the public sector, CSA works closely with GovTech and other agencies to build a core of cybersecurity specialists who will be deployed across agencies to support the Government's cybersecurity needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Douglas Foo asked how we are developing products that contribute towards a safe and trusted cyberspace for Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This Common Criteria Certificate is the de facto standard for cybersecurity product certification around the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, 30 nations, including Singapore, are part of the Common Criteria Recognition Arrangement (CCRA) for the mutual recognition of certifications.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But not all the countries are Authorising Nations where you can produce the product.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We can do it all within our economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is a step towards becoming a regional hub for product evaluation and certification.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are attracting global evaluation laboratories to anchor their operations in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These developments will accelerate Singapore’s exports of world-class cybersecurity products and create good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To encourage SMEs to build more secure products and adopt this Common Criteria certification, we have a new SecureTech track under the Accreditation@SG Digital programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Accreditation@SG Digital programme helps local SMEs to improve their business practices, engage with the local community, and be considered by Government agencies for the procurement of their products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, this new SecureTech Track will apply the same thinking towards cybersecurity SMEs and cybersecurity products for their growth, scale and their consideration by Government agencies for the procurement of cybersecurity products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Chairman, digital transformation is not only about hardware or software.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is about our citizens, workers and businesses who innovate, utilise and benefit from these technologies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our efforts span digital readiness and cybersecurity and will help these important stakeholders, so that we can embrace the potential of a common digital future together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Chairman, Minister Iswaran and Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary have shared the exciting opportunities in a digital future and what we are doing to help every Singaporean reap the digital dividend.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Digital transformation is also the key theme of enhancements to our libraries, media and Government communications, where our focus is in supporting Singaporeans in reading and learning, and in being well-informed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As Members would know, the transformation of our libraries is among the most thorough and dramatic ever experienced by our public sector agencies in their drive to serve Singaporeans better.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Beyond better collections, more comfortable surroundings and more efficient customer service, we continue to site, design and refresh libraries in a manner that keeps pace with Singaporeans' urban lifestyles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our goal is to stay ahead of changing preferences, and to continually delight library users.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We site where footfall is high, and we put extra effort into space and programme design.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: During my visit, I was heartened by the scene of students, children, working adults and grandparents reading and learning under the same roof.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Parents were guiding their children through hands-on activities based on Science, Technology, Engineering, the Arts and Mathematics (STEAM) concepts at the children's makerspace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Just a few steps away, the programme zone was bustling with seniors chatting and enjoying one another's company while picking up tips on cybersecurity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Offerings like these, combined with the library's innovative design and panoramic view of Sentosa and our port, make for a delightful visit and all-round experience for every user.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is in spite of the downward trend in visitorship and loans observed in the libraries of many other countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Over the years, we have also transformed our library collections, going beyond providing purely "books", to a vast array of learning resources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: A major push on this front has been going digital, which has redefined convenience and the reading experience for all library users.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Members of the public have written in to express their appreciation of the NLB Mobile App, launched in 2016.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Jeffery Sung discovered that within minutes of downloading the app, he was able to read newspapers from around the world and browse the bestselling books in town.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Essentially, the App has placed the library within our pockets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Singaporeans who have yet to try eBooks and audiobooks can sample them outside the library at our eReads kiosks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: NLB will roll out eight to 10 more of these kiosks across the island this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For many years, NLB has doubled the loan quota of physical items to coincide with the school holidays.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Each time we run this, we consistently get great feedback from our users, who take advantage of the promotion to read and borrow more.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I am pleased to announce that users need no longer wait for the school holidays.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Another branch in the evolution of the libraries’ collections has been expanding our local content.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Reading is a great way to deepen our love for our mother tongues and ethnic cultures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: NLB will grow its collection of localised children's books in Chinese, Malay and Tamil.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is currently shortlisting titles that Singaporean children up to the age of 12 can enjoy and relate to, for translation into vernacular languages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As Members are aware, we face a fast-changing future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In this fluctuating environment, our libraries can serve as every Singaporean’s personal learning retreat, where you can retool and enhance your personal and work life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I recently met Ms Noorjahan bte Kamaruddin, an avid learner and volunteer who inspired me in more ways than one.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To achieve her lifelong dream of publishing a recipe book, Ms Noorjahan set out to acquire skills on electronic publishing, copyright, privacy and cybersecurity matters at the "Silver Digital Creators" Workshop organised by NLB and IMDA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: She continued working on the project after the course, and is now the proud author of the eBook "Noor's Just Right Recipes".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With the knowledge she gained, she has begun training others.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Noor's story demonstrates how collaborative learning has enriched her life and the lives of others.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It also shows how technology can be harnessed by Singaporeans to achieve great things.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Dr Teo Ho Pin asked how our libraries can play a more proactive role in supporting SkillsFuture and lifelong learning.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The answer is that NLB champions continuous, self-directed learning in many ways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are making it easy for adults to take advantage of the library’s learning resources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, NLB's Digital Business Library offers more than 4,000 e-book titles condensed into 10-minute, bite-sized reads for busy adults.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I would also like to thank Dr Teo Ho Pin for his suggestion on how NLB could work more closely with SkillsFuture Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: NLB is actively partnering industries, SkillsFuture Singapore, Workforce Singapore and the Council for Third Age to deliver a comprehensive slate of job and skills-related programmes for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For instance, "SkillsFuture Advice" helps Singaporeans understand the importance of career planning and skills upgrading.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Learning today is no longer confined to information gathering, but also actively practising in a guided environment, under the tutelage of mentors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Singaporeans who are keen to tap the brains and insights of industry gamechangers, such as the founders of Carousell and ShopBack, can do so through the "Breakthrough: Conversations with Entrepreneurs and Innovators" series.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Darryl David asked how libraries can continue to serve as inclusive social spaces for Singaporeans of all ages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I am pleased to say that for all the transformation our libraries have undergone, certain principles remain constant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In the words of 29-year-old Karimah Samsudin, "The library allows you to expose yourself to different ideas, so you do not just stay in your own box or cocoon and get to know different kinds of people".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Another regular patron, Ms Leo Yih Nah, shared that book clubs were good social events that would help to lower the risk of dementia for seniors like her in the long run.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: NLB goes one step further in its aim to cultivate inclusive social spaces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is committed to extending the multitude of opportunities I have elaborated on to all, especially learners amongst us who could use an added boost.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: One of our hallmark nationwide programmes is KidsREAD, which promotes early reading for less privileged children and which celebrates its 15th anniversary this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To bring the library even closer to them, WondeRead was launched in 2018.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Similar to a subscription box delivery service, WondeRead delivers pre-loved library books quarterly to children who are not able to visit libraries on their own.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: WondeRead is accomplished with partner organisations, who either sponsored items in the box, or whose staff personally selected and packed books for each child.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Many of the WondeRead beneficiaries look forward eagerly to their next box delivery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In Mandarin):  : Our libraries are favourite go-to places for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They love to read books and newspapers in the library and nourish their mind in a cool and quiet environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is a delightful activity to complement our fast-paced urban lifestyles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Moving into the digital era, NLB will strive to provide better services for our readers, who have been very supportive of our libraries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In the digital era, the definition of books has changed and has expanded from physical and paper books to include e-books.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: People can read countless books on a small mobile phone or tablet personal computer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, avid readers need not fret about not being able to borrow as many books as they want.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The question is whether they can finish reading them all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Some of these courses are suitable for seniors and will be conducted in their mother tongue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, the Bedok Library, Toa Payoh Library and the new Harbourfront Library at Vivo City will provide these classes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I hope members of the public will give them a try.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Thirdly, to encourage children to learn their mother tongue and increase their Mother Tongue Language (MTL) reading materials, NLB will select good quality children’s books in English featuring local content, and translate them into Chinese, Malay and Tamil.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In English): Our media have an important role in helping Singaporeans stay well-informed and, through shared discourse, fostering a sense of togetherness and identity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Most Singaporeans would be able to recall growing up with their favourite local drama series, or tuning into news and current affairs programmes to follow the unfolding of national events.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Darryl David asked how PSB is evolving in response to increasing competition for eyeballs from online and foreign platforms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Indeed, PSB must keep pace with changing consumption habits so that it is integral to the lives of viewers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our national broadcaster is engaging Singaporeans across a wide range of platforms so that viewers can easily discover and enjoy local content.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Instead of the traditional approach of airing the show exclusively on television (TV), Mediacorp released content on an array of platforms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: On top of the 1.7 million viewers who tuned in on Free-to-Air TV, more than 850,000 watched it on Toggle.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Performance tracks were streamed more than 150,000 times on major digital music platforms, such as Spotify, and social media and on-ground outreach events extended engagement further still.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Another important priority of ours is to strengthen the reach of local vernacular content.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In Mandarin):  : In order to help the public access more information in Chinese and expand their audience base in the digital era, Mediacorp has pooled resources in TV and radio to create a new portal that includes news, entertainment and lifestyle information, and this is set to be launched in the middle of the year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In English): Suria will continue to partner with community organisations in large-scale events, such as the opening of Wisma Geylang Serai.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In the same vein, Vasantham is partnering the Tamil Language Council and Tamil Language Learning and Promotion Committee for community events like the annual Tamil Language Festival.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Through ground events and engagement, Suria and Vasantham are able to connect with their communities and celebrate culture and values, while increasing social media outreach and the visibility of their content and artistes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: From listening to citizens’ views and concerns, to explaining Government policies and schemes, the Ministry builds clear channels for communication that foster a well-informed and engaged nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling asked how we can improve communications of Government policies across age groups and communities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Rather than a one-size-fits-all approach, we customise the content, platforms and languages for different groups of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For our millennials, we produced a web series Ah Boys – Hidden Warfare, that covered topics of concern to them, like jobs and economy, and marriage and parenthood.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For older audiences, there was the Getai Challenge, where we adapted the skits and music performances of a familiar local tradition to share useful information with our seniors, such as housing, social support measures and diabetes awareness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Age is not the only diversity we cater for.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our communications are also tailored for various communities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, we rode on the festive cheer of the Deepavali and Chinese New Year seasons to share timely and informative content with our Indian and Chinese communities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Similarly, we customised programmes, such as Abang Teksi, which highlighted different forms of Government assistance to help Singaporeans tide through disruptions, including Adapt and Grow initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Leon Perera asked about public opinion surveys conducted by the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Government agencies use a variety of means to better understand ground issues and concerns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These include outreach activities conducted by REACH, house visits and surveys which help our agencies assess public sentiment on issues, and public awareness of, and response to, Government policies and programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Most surveys that MCI and other agencies conduct are for internal reference, like the ones I have described.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government does not compile statistics on the surveys conducted by various agencies, or which among them are published.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In MCI, REACH periodically releases survey data on a range of issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In recent years, REACH has released surveys of public perceptions on the annual Budget and the National Day Rally Speech, Central Provident Fund changes, public transport and the public's awareness of financial assistance schemes, among other subjects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These survey findings may also be found on REACH's website.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government does not make policy decisions or decide communication strategies solely on the basis of surveys.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But they help ensure that service delivery and policy implementation are satisfactory.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government releases surveys that may be of interest to the public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, REACH has released surveys of public perception on the Annual Budget and the National Day Rally speech, fake news and public transport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Another example would be the study of social capital commissioned by MCCY.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Other surveys released include studies of youth, national security awareness as well as attitudes towards water conservation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As for coordination, agencies need the operational flexibility to conduct their own surveys on issues of concern within their purview.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Some questions may be common across different surveys because they are cross-cutting in nature.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our agencies coordinate such efforts when it is operationally feasible to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Darryl David asked how we can improve civic discussion in schools and beyond to encourage the plurality of views among Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Through public consultations, Singaporeans have a say in shaping public policies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: More than 36,000 Singaporeans have provided feedback on issues like the cost of living, jobs, transport and fake news, at more than 250 REACH Listening Points and dialogues between 2017 and 2018.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: REACH regularly engages students on national issues at dedicated Listening Points and dialogues held at our IHLs as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Among them was university student, Mr Alif Mohammad Hafidz, who gave his suggestions to this year's Budget and shared that the session motivated him to find out more about the Budget process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will continue to consult the public on issues of importance to our nation’s future and invite Singaporeans to lend their voices to the ongoing dialogue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Chairman, I have described how my Ministry plans to help Singaporeans stay connected and engaged, through reading, learning and being well-informed, and how digital transformation will play a key role in these plans.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, many Members have spoken in this COS debate about the need to bring Singaporeans closer together as we take Singapore forward.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Through the media sector, we will engage Singaporeans with shared stories of our home and nation.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Through our National Library and Archives, we will cultivate a shared appreciation of our past, so that we can move into the future with confidence and a strong sense of our identity.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The digital age offers great promise for our media sector to grow.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: There is a discernible shift towards Asia and Asian content.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We are at the confluence of the East and the West.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We have talented storytellers and world-class digital infrastructure.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We must leverage these strengths to develop promising young talent, deepen the skills of our media workforce and prime our industry to ride the wave of growth in the global media ecosystem.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Darryl David has asked about our plans to develop the local media industry.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We are doing so through manpower development plans like our Skills Framework for Media, which maps out career pathways and skills to help media professionals stay ahead of the competition.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We will enhance this Framework to meet the industry's needs for writing and storytelling skills, as well as the demand for professionals with digital skills like data analytics and social media management.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Next, we will strengthen on-the-job training to familiarise fresh media professionals with the latest trends and tools of the trade.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: IMDA will launch a Story Lab Apprenticeship this year to help young media professionals gain customised training and experience in key media companies.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I am glad that companies like Mediacorp, mm2 Entertainment, HBO Asia and Turner Asia Pacific have already expressed interest to come on board.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: IMDA will announce more details by the third quarter of this year.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We will also help media professionals master digital skills to compete and thrive in today's landscape.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Our CET courses have been very useful to media professionals like 37-year-old Ms Nusaibah Abdul Rahim, who is creative director of a media production company.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Last December, Ms Nusaibah attended a data-driven content development workshop organised by the Singapore Media Academy and learned how to analyse data from audience insights to drive creative decision-making.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: IMDA will curate more of such CET courses.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Darryl David asked about our plans to help local media companies go global.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In other words, content, but it is digital first.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: IMDA's funding call for proposals will close by the end of this month, and I strongly encourage local companies to make use of this resource.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We will expand the Singapore Media Festival to seize the opportunities created by the growing convergence of the tech and media industries and strengthen Singapore's thought leadership in the region.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: IMDA will share more details in the second quarter of this year.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Our efforts to develop the media industry will help us tell our stories better to our fellow Singaporeans and to the rest of the world.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And there is, indeed, no better story one could argue than the story of Singapore.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This year’s Bicentennial commemoration will help us to understand our early history, how Raffles' landing in 1819 set us on a path to where we are today, and reflect on the attributes we will need to succeed in the future.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The National Library and Archives will play an important and meaningful role in this Bicentennial commemoration.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: NLB will roll out a series of activities to increase engagement with Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: For example, NLB's librarians will play host and present the National Library's rare material collection with 25 specially produced videos.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Some highlights of this valuable treasure trove of Singapore's early history include Munajathu Thiratuu, the oldest Tamil book on Islamic religious poetry held by the National Library, or Hikayat Abdullah, one of the most important records of the sociopolitical landscape in Singapore, Malacca and the southern Malay kingdoms at the turn of the 19th century.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: These videos will be released every fortnight from April on NLB's social media channels.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We have also brought a special preview of the NLB's archives to Parliament.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I invite all Members to visit the Reception Hall of Parliament House to view exhibits that showcase our multicultural roots and life in early Singapore.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: NLB has also worked with community groups to digitise valuable historical content.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Last month, Senior Minister of State Sim Ann launched the Singapore Biographical Database of Chinese Personalities to remember Pioneers who contributed significantly to Singapore in its early days.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: NLB and the Tamil Digital Heritage Group are already hard at work collecting historical materials on Indian dance in Singapore for a new Digital Archive of Singapore's Tamil Dance.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Our National Archives also have much to offer.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The National Archives Singapore (NAS) celebrated their Golden Jubilee last year, and their birthday wish is to encourage every Singaporean to play a part in preserving our collective memories.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: One such volunteer interviewer is 31-year-old Ms Sushma Somasekharan, an auditor and classical Indian vocalist who recently interviewed her first music teacher, the accomplished Carnatic singer Dr Bhagya Murthy.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Thanks to Ms Sushma's interview, we gained valuable insight into the Indian classical music scene in the 1980s and how it evolved with a uniquely Singaporean twist because, in those days, Dr Murthy apparently had to learn to sing in Malay and Mandarin to cater to a multiracial audience as well.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: NAS will also launch an online system that allows members of the public to request digital images of Singapore in its early days.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I hope these commemorative events will ignite the interest and passion among Singaporeans to discover more about our past and ourselves.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Chairman, the NLB and NAS have done tremendous work as custodians of Singapore's heritage and memories.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I hope that Members felt more than a tinge of nostalgia watching those images.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Chairman, my Ministry will continue to create opportunities for all Singaporeans in a digital economy and help Singaporeans of all ages embrace technology.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We will endeavour to keep our cyberspace safe and secure and enhance Government communications to foster an engaged Singapore.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Through the efforts of the National Library and Archives, we will foster a deep understanding of our shared journey from the past to the present and aspire to build a better Singapore, our home, in the next 200 years and beyond.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We look forward to working closely with all Singaporeans as MCI perseveres in its mission to connect Singaporeans to one another and to a better and brighter future.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: (In Mandarin):  : 	I would like to thank the Minister for the reply.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: First, Singapore is determined to realise the vision of a Smart Nation.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: However, amongst Singaporeans, there is still a generation of senior citizens who need our help to pick up digital technology.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: My second question is that communicating policies is an art, and the Minister had earlier shared with us that policies are being communicated to our people through multimedia and television programmes.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: For senior citizens, television programmes may just be a one-off event, and they may miss out on some of the important explanations and information.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: I suggest that we repeat these important messages and spread them to all corners of the community so that our citizens, particularly our senior citizens, will understand the policymaking process and considerations behind these policies.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: In this way, Singaporeans will have a better understanding of the thought process behind the Government’s decisions and may give stronger support to our policies.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: I hope the Senior Minister of State can elaborate on that.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: (In Mandarin):  :  I thank the Member for her clarification.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: She asked about how we can help senior citizens embrace digital technology.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Indeed, it is our hope that all senior citizens in Singapore will be able to ride the wave of the digital era and become savvy in digital technology.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In terms of courses and training, there are two important points to note for seniors.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Another point is that the programmes must be tailored for beginners and the pace must not be too fast.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We take note of these two important points.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: They offer opportunities for our senior citizens to learn digital and ICT in a relaxing and comfortable environment.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This takes into account the fact that many of our senior citizens prefer to learn from instructors on a one-to-one basis.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In addition, there are technology touchpoints available at eight community clubs, where our PA counter staff provide one-to-one assistance to residents and help them learn to use electronic devices and services.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The libraries have also introduced a new Seniors Tech and Read programme to teach senior citizens to borrow electronic books and access the Internet.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, we hope that our senior citizens will also be able to enjoy the convenience of e-books.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We have been working hard on the communication of our policies and engagement of the public.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We would like to take this opportunity to encourage our Parliamentary colleagues to make good use of all the budget-related information provided by the Ministry of Finance (MOF).

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Nowadays, there are more and more information available in the four official languages with richer content.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We hope that beyond textual information, the Powerpoint slide shows with voice-over explanations made available by MOF will help our people better understand various policies.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This is an example of how ongoing communication efforts can complement one-off television or radio programmes to reinforce Singaporeans’ impression of important policies.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Mr Chairman, I have two points of clarification.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: The first point I believe should be for Senior Minister of State Sim Ann because it pertains to the library and digital books.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: I just wanted to ask the Senior Minister of State if she could update on some trends on e-books or digital book borrowing.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: And does she see a trend in e-book or digital book perhaps even outstripping conventional publications of books in the long run?

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Second point of clarification is for, I believe, could be for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: And I really have to commend the National Archives team on the wonderful job that was done.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: I was wondering if the National Archives could perhaps engage other Government agencies, say, MOE, for example, to ensure that all the excellent work that has been done could also be shared with our students in primary and secondary schools.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: In the past, this would involve an excursion to the National Archives building and I believe that might be the case for some materials.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: But I believe much of what I saw as digitalised can be brought onto screens and into the schools.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: So, is that something that perhaps the Minister could consider, in terms of exposing more of our younger Singaporeans to all of this rich history?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Indeed, we have seen very rapid growth in the use of e-books amongst our library users.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, I think it is a situation in which e-books and e-loans are growing rapidly.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: But I would say that physical books are still very dominant.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As to whether one will outstrip the other, that remains to be seen.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: But what is clear is that NLB very much should be with the e-books trend to ensure that while they take care of readers who prefer physical books, at the same time, we have to ensure that our collections of e-books and newspapers and magazines continue to be enriched.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Chairman, I think it is a very useful insight from Senior Minister of State Sim Ann's earlier reply.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In fact, the digital platforms are very effective in reaching certain demographics.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And the growth in e-books and the borrowings are largely being driven by a younger demographic.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But I think, in general, as Senior Minister of State Sim Ann says, borrowings in physical books also continues to hold its own.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, I think we are in a good situation and we want to encourage the reading habit through whichever channels in order to broaden the reach.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In that vein, the Member's second question about the National Archives, we agree with him fully.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, videos, which will be put out by NLB through its platforms, are going to be one important channel.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In fact, much of the Archives' material is already available digitally.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We will certainly pursue the option of seeing how we can go in in a more targeted way, for example, to schools.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But at the same time, I would just urge all Members to also propagate the message.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I am sure all Members have downloaded the NLB app and are using it actively.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And I hope then that you will also continue to share that experience with all your constituents and others you are interacting with.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: From the Senior Minister of State's reply, she cited some examples of opinion polls that had been released.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I assume that some of these Government opinion polls are for internal reference and are not released.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: So, my point of clarification would be what would be the concern or impediment or issue with making it a more general rule to release the results of all such surveys, unless there are strong reasons not to, such as national security, such as sensitive issues of sorts, to release that information to the public domain for stakeholders to use?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As I have mentioned just now in the speech, the Government releases results of surveys that may be of interest to the public.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, these would be some of the reasons, for instance, why not all survey results would be released to the public.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Chairman, I have a question for Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: He had earlier given a very descriptive plan of the cybersecurity state of affairs in Singapore and I wanted to just understand a little bit more about how we are assessing or measuring the savviness of our people in dealings in cyberspace because it would be useful to actually understand where some of the weak points are.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The Senior Minister of State mentioned earlier about issues with regard to using lax passwords, phishing and all that.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Clearly, there are some areas where we could improve on and I appreciate the efforts by the Media Literacy Council as well as the NLB with SURE.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But are there some areas that we could look at on how we can measure and assess and target some of the efforts so that we can improve cybersecurity in Singapore?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Ms Rahayu Mahzam for the question.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We do not really know what would catch fire.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In a way, we try to, by looking to see when things go wrong, such as scams, cyber breaches or theft of information, and so on and so forth.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, we can measure when things go wrong.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But that is not necessarily a good example of how savvy we are, which is the word that the Member used.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Internationally, people have tried to develop these measures around knowledge.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, how if you take a poll, for example, whether it is secondary school students or early adults or across the population segment, what do people know about it?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Then, you can perhaps also look and see, for example, what are the products and services that businesses would use, either knowledge within the business community or the use of protective technologies within the various communities.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And people have tried to come up with these types of measures.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And on these types of measures, we come up very well, but that is not something to pat ourselves on the back and assume that there will be no problem.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Actually, we do have to keep reminding ourselves.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The key issues are really human behaviour and the social factors.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary

text: One of the points which I raised was about the work of PDPC in helping to achieve outcomes for complainants.
